Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Revision contracts and explicit conversion

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Use these cold-path tools before changing a saved or networked value type. They freeze representation contracts; they do not infer compatible gameplay behavior.

Odin
source, report := evolution.freeze(Old_World, "game_revision_12", "World_12")
// source is owned; write only after report.error == .None, then delete(source).
manifest, report := evolution.contract(Old_World, CONTENT_12)
scaffold, report := evolution.scaffold(Old_World, New_World,
    "game_revision_conversion", "World_12", "World_13")

freeze recursively emits all type dependencies into one self-contained Odin type. It retains field names/tags, fixed array bounds, scalar widths, enum names/values and bit-set definitions. It normalizes native layout and endianness: Replay's canonical encoding, not memcpy layout, is the contract. No imports of live game types remain. Choose globally unique Odin package names for different revisions.

Supported shapes are canonical scalars, structs, fixed arrays, enums and bit sets. Unions, enumerated arrays and unsupported shapes fail with an owned diagnostic and no generated source. Existing schema union support remains available; freeze those revisions with explicitly authored source until a union-aware generator is provided. This tool uses the complete authority projection.

contract returns owned JSON containing the semantic ID, schema fingerprint, canonical schema text and leaf field paths/kinds/widths/wire offsets, privacy, enum meaning and bit masks. Check it into source control beside the frozen type. Compare regenerated manifests in CI. It does not freeze reducer code, authorize an old recording for a new reducer, or replace a signed build manifest.

scaffold handles additive schema changes. Its generated procedure deliberately returns failure until the author supplies target defaults and changes the review flag. Every added leaf is listed by full path, including every array element. Removed fields, changed widths/kinds, enum meanings/signedness, privacy changes and unions/enumerated arrays require custom authored conversion code instead of an automatic scaffold.

Odin
defaults := New_Catalog{} // Deliberate decision: old enemies gain no pulse attack.
paths := []string{"$.enemy.pulse.windup", "$.enemy.pulse.damage"}
value, report := evolution.copy_preserved(old, defaults, paths)
report = evolution.verify_preserved(old, value, paths)

copy_preserved validates both values, copies matching canonical leaf bytes into the supplied target defaults and decodes transactionally. It requires exactly one acknowledgement for every added field and rejects extra/duplicate acknowledgements. It does not validate game invariants: call the target model's validator before publishing a checkpoint. verify_preserved checks every old leaf; separately assert the chosen new defaults. remove_added provides an explicit inverse projection for fixture builders, acknowledging each discarded leaf.

These helpers compile schemas, allocate scratch and use linear path lookup within field loops. They are intended for authoring, offline upgrades and tests, not the simulation tick or a per-frame presentation path.

Scrapyard demonstrates this with a fully frozen content49, its committed contract, and the actual content49→50 checkpoint converter. Run:

Shell
mkdir -p /absolute/staging/revision
nix develop --command odin run examples/replay_scrapyard/tools/revision \
  -collection:godot=. -- /absolute/staging/revision
nix develop --command odin test tests/replay_evolution -collection:godot=.

The example command writes a reviewable pair of frozen catalogs, JSON contracts and a disabled conversion scaffold into the staging directory. Review before adopting them; retain the historical reducer and real old-file fixtures.
